key_insight: The paper shows that disruption response in supply chains can be improved by combining ADMM-based distributed re-optimization with LLM-guided discovery of outside capacity offers from unstructured provider profiles.
engineering_relevance: For logistics and operations teams, this suggests a practical way to find and integrate hidden capacity without fully exposing incumbent models or requiring a complete structured supplier registry.
method: Model open capacity pooling as a network-membership decision after disruption.
Use ADMM to coordinate incumbents while preserving model privacy.
Direct LLM-based profile search with residual capacity gaps, then verify offers and re-optimize with warm starts.
evidence_signal: Across 200 synthetic episodes, full-information opening recovered 24.6% of capacity-scarcity cost, while 40-contact coordination-directed search with LLM ranking captured 32.0% of that value versus 4.7% for undirected contact.
watch_item: The approach is only optimal when every eligible offer is revealed at exact prices, and performance depends on the quality of profile indexing, extraction, and offer disclosure.
paper_title: Open Capacity Pooling in Agentic Supply Chains: Coordination-Directed LLM Discovery and Distributed Re-optimization
